title: API key is shipped in client-side JavaScript and sent as a Bearer token from the browser
evidence: api.js:3 defines the key; api.js:6 and api.js:11 attach it to the Authorization header. index.html:25 serves api.js to every visitor. README.md:6 claims the key never leaves the server.
failing_case: Anyone who opens the page views source or DevTools, copies the key, and calls POST /v1/refunds directly with any ids. The key authorises refunds, so this moves money.
remediation: Move the key to a server-side proxy that authenticates the dashboard user and enforces refund limits. Rotate the key that was shipped.

quote: fetch(`${API_BASE}/refunds`, { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: "[redacted]" + API_KEY, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ ids }) });
title: refund() does not await the request and always returns { ok: true }
evidence: api.js:11 calls fetch without await and without a catch. api.js:12 returns { ok: true } at once. app.js:50-51 treats that as success and shows the toast.
failing_case: The user is offline, the key is rejected (401) or the server returns 500. The toast still says 'Refunded 3 orders!'. The customers are not refunded and the operator believes they are. A network error also raises an unhandled promise rejection.
remediation: await the fetch, check res.ok, return the parsed result or throw. In app.js catch the error and show the cause and a retry action. Show success only after a 2xx.

title: Customer name, id and status from the API are written into innerHTML unescaped
evidence: app.js:32 interpolates o.customer.name, o.id and o.status into an HTML string assigned with innerHTML. Nothing escapes them. The page also holds the API key in the same origin (api.js:3).
failing_case: A customer registers with the name . Any staff member who loads the dashboard runs the script, which reads API_KEY and can POST to /refunds.
remediation: Build rows with createElement and textContent, or escape every interpolated value in one helper. Set data-id through dataset.

title: Selection only ever grows: unchecking never removes an id, so unchecked orders are still refunded
evidence: app.js:35 pushes on check and has no else branch. selected (app.js:5) is never cleared by renderTable, load or the refund handler (app.js:49-52). Rows are re-rendered on page and filter changes, so checkboxes reset while selected keeps stale ids.
failing_case: Tick order 7, untick it, tick order 9, click Refund. selected is ['7','9'], so order 7 is refunded as well. Also: tick an order, type in the search box so it leaves the list, click Refund. The hidden order is still refunded. Ticking twice sends duplicates.
remediation: Keep selected as a Set. Add on check and delete on uncheck. Re-check boxes from the set on render. Clear it after a confirmed refund, and drop ids not in the current result on load.

quote: - **Pricing:** the Team plan is $15 per seat; 12 seats on annual billing at 20% off is $1,440 a year.
title: Pricing arithmetic is wrong: 12 seats at $15 a month with 20% off is $1,728 a year
evidence: Recomputed: 15 x 12 seats = $180 a month; x 12 months = $2,160; less 20% = $1,728. $1,440 matches neither the monthly nor the annual figure unless the seat count or discount is different. The README also does not say $15 is per month.
failing_case: A customer or sales rep quotes $1,440 a year and the invoice is $288 higher.
remediation: State the period of the seat price and correct the total to $1,728, or correct the inputs if $1,440 was meant. Better, drop pricing from a dashboard README.

title: Text contrast is below 4.5:1 in the stat labels, the Prev/Next buttons and the eyebrow
evidence: Computed: #aaa on #fff (styles.css:9, label on card) is about 2.3:1. #aaa on #F4F1EA (styles.css:18, the pager buttons, 12 px) is about 2.1:1. #c7c2f0 on the #6366f1 end of the gradient (styles.css:4 on :3) is about 2.6:1. All are small text. WCAG 1.4.3 (AA).
failing_case: REVENUE, ORDERS and AVG ORDER labels and the Prev and Next buttons are hard to read for low-vision users and in bright light; the pager controls look disabled when they are live.
remediation: Use at least #595959 on white and on the cream page background for those texts, raise the eyebrow to white or a lighter tint, and raise the 11-12 px text to at least 14 px.

quote: - **Fully accessible:** meets WCAG 2.1 AA, including 44 px touch targets (criterion 2.5.5).
title: README claims WCAG 2.1 AA and 44 px targets; the code fails AA and 2.5.5 is AAA, not AA
evidence: Contradicted by the findings at index.html:19 (span as button), styles.css:19 (no focus outline), styles.css:9 (contrast), styles.css:13 (reflow). Prev/Next buttons are 12 px text with 2px 4px padding (styles.css:18), well under 44 px. In WCAG 2.1, 2.5.5 is a Level AAA criterion.
failing_case: A procurement or legal reader relies on the stated AA conformance. The page fails several AA criteria and one A criterion, so the claim is false and the criterion level is wrong.
remediation: Remove the claim or replace it with a measured statement of what was tested. Fix the failures first.

quote: - **Secure:** the API key never leaves the server.
title: README says the API key stays on the server; it is hard-coded in the browser script
evidence: api.js:3 holds the key and index.html:25 serves it to every client. api.js:6 sends it from the browser.
failing_case: A reader trusts the line and does not rotate or restrict the key. Anyone viewing source has it.
remediation: Fix the code (server-side proxy), then keep or reword the claim.

title: getOrders never checks the HTTP status; a failure leaves the dashboard broken with no message
evidence: api.js:6-7 returns res.json() whatever the status. app.js:41 assigns it to orders and app.js:42 renders. load() (app.js:38-43) has no try/catch.
failing_case: The API answers 401 or 500 with { error: 'x' }. orders is an object, so orders.length is undefined, the 'for ... of' in renderStats throws TypeError, and the table and cards keep their old or empty content. If the network is down, fetch rejects as an unhandled rejection. The user sees nothing and cannot tell the data is stale.
remediation: Check res.ok and Array.isArray, throw with the status. In load() catch, show an error banner with a Retry button and keep the last good data marked as stale.

title: Pagination is off by one: the first ten orders are never shown on load, and Prev/Next are unbounded
evidence: page starts at 1 (app.js:3) and start = page * PAGE_SIZE (app.js:27) is 10, so orders 0-9 are skipped. app.js:34 prints 'Page 1 of floor(n/10)', which drops the last partial page (n=25 gives 'of 2' with 3 pages of data) and gives 'of 0' for under 10 orders. app.js:47-48 never clamp page. page is not reset to the first page when the search or status changes (app.js:38-43).
failing_case: 20 orders load: the table shows orders 11-20 under 'Page 1 of 2'. Orders 1-10 appear only after clicking Prev, which shows 'Page 0 of 2'. Click Prev again: page -1 gives a negative slice start and wrong rows. With 5 orders the table is empty and the label reads 'Page 1 of 0'.
remediation: Use (page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE, total pages = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(n / PAGE_SIZE)), clamp page, disable Prev/Next at the ends and reset page to 1 in load().

title: Order status is shown only as a coloured dot with no text
evidence: app.js:32 renders an empty span. styles.css:16-17 colour it green, red or yellow (#3c3, #c33, #cc3). WCAG 1.4.1 (A) and 1.1.1.
failing_case: A colour-blind user cannot tell paid from refunded (red/green). A screen reader user hears nothing for the Status column. Refunded and paid are the two states this page is about.
remediation: Print the status word in the cell, with the dot as decoration (aria-hidden).

title: Refund runs on one click with no confirmation, no empty check and no double-submit guard; README says refunds are confirmed
evidence: app.js:49-52 calls refund(selected) directly. No confirm dialog, no disabled state during the call, no check that selected is non-empty. README.md:9 states 'Refunds are confirmed before they are sent'.
failing_case: Click Refund selected twice quickly with 3 orders selected: two POSTs go out with the same ids. Click it with nothing selected: a POST goes out with an empty list and the toast says 'Refunded 0 orders!'.
remediation: Disable the control and ignore clicks while a request is in flight, refuse an empty selection with a message, and ask for confirmation naming the count and total. Send an idempotency key.

title: Search box, status select and row checkboxes have no accessible name
evidence: index.html:17-18 have no label or aria-label; the placeholder disappears on typing. app.js:32 renders each row's checkbox with no label. index.html:21 has an empty <th></th>. WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2.
failing_case: A screen reader user hears 'edit text' and 'combo box' and, for every row, 'checkbox' with no customer name, so they cannot tell which order they are selecting for a refund.
remediation: Add <label for=q>, <label for=status> (or aria-label), aria-label="Select order from NAME" on each checkbox, and visually hidden text in the empty header cell.

title: The primary action is a span: not focusable, no button role, not operable by keyboard or screen reader
evidence: index.html:19 is a span with an onclick set in app.js:49. It has no tabindex, role or key handling. WCAG 2.1.1 (A) and 4.1.2 (A).
failing_case: A keyboard-only user tabs through the page: focus goes search, status, Prev, Next and never lands on Refund selected. A screen reader announces plain text, not a button. This user cannot refund anything.
remediation: Use <button type="button" id="refundBtn">, with a disabled state when nothing is selected, and style it with a visible :focus-visible ring.

quote: table { width: 1000px; border-collapse: collapse; background: #fff; border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.1); }
title: Table is a fixed 1000 px wide and the stat cards stay three across, so the page scrolls sideways on a phone
evidence: styles.css:13 fixes width at 1000px. styles.css:6 forces repeat(3, 1fr) cards at any width. styles.css:15 clips the name column at 120 px with no ellipsis. There is no media query. WCAG 1.4.10 reflow (AA).
failing_case: At 390 px the table overflows by about 600 px and the user must scroll horizontally to reach the status column. At 200% zoom on a 1360 px screen the same happens. Long names are cut off mid-word with no hint.
remediation: Use width:100% with a wrapper that has overflow-x:auto, or stack rows into cards below 600 px; make .cards auto-fit minmax(160px,1fr); add text-overflow: ellipsis and a title on names.

title: Focus outline is removed from every control with no replacement
evidence: styles.css:19 sets outline none for button, input and select and defines no other focus style. WCAG 2.4.7 (AA).
failing_case: Tab to Prev, Next, the search box or the status select: nothing changes on screen, so a keyboard user cannot see where focus is.
remediation: Delete the rule, or replace it with :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid; outline-offset: 2px } at 3:1 contrast against its neighbours.

title: Performance claim has no measurement and the code does not support it
evidence: load() fetches the whole list on every keystroke (app.js:41, no debounce at app.js:45), renderStats walks every order each time (app.js:11) and the page has no benchmark. Only 10 rows are drawn per page, so 'renders 10,000' is not what the code does either.
failing_case: With 10,000 orders the user downloads and parses the full JSON on each keystroke. The README promises 'instantly' with no number or test behind it.
remediation: Measure it (time to first render and per keystroke at 10,000 rows) and state the number, or remove the claim. Move search and paging to the server.

quote: const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/orders?q=${query}&status=${status}`, { headers: { Authorization: "[redacted]" + API_KEY } });
title: Search text is put into the query string without encoding
evidence: api.js:6 interpolates query and status raw. query comes from the search box (app.js:39).
failing_case: Type "a&status=refunded" or "x#": the typed & and # end the q value and inject or truncate parameters, so the search returns the wrong set. Searching for 'Smith & Sons' sends q=Smith  and a stray parameter.
remediation: Build the URL with URLSearchParams, or wrap each value in encodeURIComponent.

title: Tax rate, loyalty discount and revenue rules are hard-coded inside a render function
evidence: app.js:9-17 computes 8.25% tax, a 10% gold discount and the paid-minus-refunded rule inside renderStats. The table (app.js:32) shows raw o.total, so the card total and the visible rows disagree. Floating-point money is summed and then rounded only at display (app.js:20).
failing_case: A gold customer with a $100.00 paid order is shown as $100 in the table, but the revenue card counts $97.43. The revenue card never matches the sum of visible rows. Rates changed by finance require editing view code. The discount is also applied to a refund, which may not match what was originally charged.
remediation: Move revenue into one pure, tested function (integer cents, named constants for tax and discount) and have both the cards and the table use it. Confirm with the owner whether the tax and discount belong on the client at all.

title: Empty result gives 'NaN' in the Average Order card and an empty table with no explanation
evidence: app.js:18 divides by orders.length with no guard. app.js:22 prints avg.toFixed(2). renderTable renders zero rows with no empty message (app.js:31-34).
failing_case: Search for a name that matches nothing. The cards show '$0.00', '0' and '$NaN', and the table body is blank with 'Page 1 of 0'. The same happens on first run with no orders.
remediation: Return 0 when there are no orders and show 'No orders match. Clear the search or choose All.' with a clear-filters button.

title: Every keystroke fires a request and responses are applied in arrival order
evidence: app.js:45 binds load to oninput with no debounce, and app.js:41-42 applies whatever response arrives last. No abort and no sequence check.
failing_case: Type 'smith' quickly. Requests for 's', 'sm', 'smi' ... are in flight. The response for 'sm' returns after the response for 'smith', so the table shows results for 'sm' while the box shows 'smith'. The user can then tick and refund rows from the wrong result set.
remediation: Debounce input by about 250 ms and use an AbortController per load, or ignore responses whose sequence number is not the latest.

title: Toast is not announced to screen readers and never dismisses
evidence: index.html:23 has no role=status or aria-live. app.js:51 sets display block and never hides it, so a second refund rewrites the same visible text with no change a user could notice. WCAG 4.1.3 (AA).
failing_case: A screen reader user clicks refund (if they could reach it) and hears nothing. A sighted user sees the toast stay on screen over the table corner indefinitely, with no close control.
remediation: Add role="status" aria-live="polite" to the element, and hide it after a timeout or add a Dismiss button. Show errors with role="alert".

title: Toast pulses forever and ignores prefers-reduced-motion
evidence: styles.css:20 sets an infinite animation and styles.css:21 defines the keyframes. No prefers-reduced-motion block exists. WCAG 2.3.3 / 2.2.2.
failing_case: After a refund, the toast scales up and down every second until the page is reloaded. A user with vestibular sensitivity who has reduced motion on still sees it.
remediation: Remove the animation, or run it once and wrap it in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference).
